text.p: Sugen Inc and Allergan Inc said Tuesday they entered into a deal to develop and commercialize novel pharmaceutical compounds for the treatment of ophthalmic diseases.

During the collaboration, Allergan will be Sugen's exclusive corporate partner in the ophthalmic field and will have rights to all ophthalmic uses of collaboration products and technology worldwide, the companies said.

Allergan said it will pay Sugen a $2 million technology set-up fee and will purchase $4 million of Sugen common stock at $20.88 a share. Allergan also plans to purchase $3 million of Sugen common stock at the market price of Sugen's next equity offering.
Sugen will receive research and drug discovery funding for three years, as well as milestone payments and royalties on worldwide sales of any collaboration products, the companies said.

Sugen also will have the right to contribute to phase II/III clinical development costs on each program. This will allow Sugen to earn profits from successful collaboration products in North America and Europe, the companies said.
